events.title: Gregory VII's synod condemns married and simoniac priests
events.description: At his Lenten synod in Rome, Pope Gregory VII barred married priests and those who had bought office from ministering. The reforms helped impose clerical celibacy in the Western Church.
events.html: At his Lenten synod in Rome, Pope Gregory VII barred married priests and those who had bought office from ministering. The reforms helped impose clerical celibacy in the Western Church.

events.title: Pedro Álvares Cabral sails from Lisbon
events.description: Cabral's fleet of 13 ships left for India, swinging far west into the Atlantic. On 22 April it sighted the coast of Brazil, which Cabral claimed for Portugal.
events.html: Cabral's fleet of 13 ships left for India, swinging far west into the Atlantic. On 22 April it sighted the coast of Brazil, which Cabral claimed for Portugal.

events.title: Napoleon Bonaparte marries Joséphine de Beauharnais
events.description: The civil wedding in Paris took place two days before Napoleon left to command the Army of Italy. Joséphine became empress in 1804, but he divorced her in 1810 for lack of an heir.
events.html: The civil wedding in Paris took place two days before Napoleon left to command the Army of Italy. Joséphine became empress in 1804, but he divorced her in 1810 for lack of an heir.

events.title: Supreme Court frees the Amistad Africans
events.description: The Court ruled that the Mende captives who had seized the slave ship Amistad had been illegally enslaved. Argued by John Quincy Adams, the case became a cause for abolitionists.

events.title: Monitor and Virginia fight the first battle between ironclads
events.description: At Hampton Roads, Virginia, USS Monitor and the Confederate CSS Virginia fought for hours without decisive damage. The duel showed that wooden warships were obsolete.
events.html: At Hampton Roads, Virginia, USS Monitor and the Confederate CSS Virginia fought for hours without decisive damage. The duel showed that wooden warships were obsolete.

events.title: Pancho Villa raids Columbus, New Mexico
events.description: Some 500 of Villa's fighters attacked the border town, killing 18 Americans. The US sent General John Pershing on a punitive expedition into Mexico, which failed to catch Villa.
events.html: Some 500 of Villa's fighters attacked the border town, killing 18 Americans. The US sent General John Pershing on a punitive expedition into Mexico, which failed to catch Villa.

events.title: US firebombing raid devastates Tokyo
events.description: In the night of 9-10 March, some 300 B-29 bombers dropped incendiaries on Tokyo, burning about 41 square kilometres. Around 100,000 people died, the deadliest air raid in history.
